items.followUp: State two differences between Rutherford’s and Bohr’s atomic models, including what happens to an electron’s energy.

rubric.why: Rutherford’s model has electrons revolving around the nucleus and, according to classical theory, radiating energy.
rubric.description: States Rutherford’s electron motion and energy loss
rubric.how: Award for stating that Rutherford’s revolving electrons radiate energy.

rubric.why: Continuous energy loss would make an electron’s orbit shrink, rendering Rutherford’s atom unstable.
rubric.description: Explains the instability of Rutherford’s atom
rubric.how: Award for stating that the electron would fall into the nucleus or that Rutherford’s model could not explain atomic stability.

rubric.why: Bohr’s model introduced specific allowed orbits with definite energies.
rubric.how: Award for stating that Bohr’s electrons occupy specific fixed orbits or energy levels.

rubric.why: Electrons in Bohr’s stationary orbits do not continuously lose energy.
rubric.description: States the energy behaviour in Bohr’s orbits
rubric.how: Award for stating that electrons do not radiate energy while in an allowed stationary orbit.

accept: jumps from one orbit to another
rubric.why: Bohr’s model explains energy exchange when an electron moves between allowed orbits.
rubric.description: States energy exchange during an orbit transition
rubric.how: Award for stating that an electron absorbs or emits energy when it jumps between orbits.

modelAnswer: Rutherford proposed that electrons revolve around the nucleus and continuously radiate energy.
As an electron loses energy, its orbit would shrink and it would eventually fall into the nucleus; thus Rutherford’s model could not explain the stability of atoms.
Bohr proposed that electrons revolve in specific fixed orbits, each with a definite energy.
Electrons in these stationary orbits do not radiate energy.
An electron absorbs or emits energy when it jumps from one orbit to another.

rubric.why: Industrial chemistry concerns the processes and methods used to manufacture chemical substances on an industrial scale.
rubric.how: Award for identifying industrial-scale manufacture or the processes used for it.

rubric.why: Analytical chemistry identifies the components of substances and determines their composition.
rubric.how: Award for describing the identification of components or determination of a substance’s composition.

modelAnswer: Industrial chemistry is the branch of chemistry that deals with methods and processes used to manufacture chemical substances on an industrial scale.
Analytical chemistry is the branch of chemistry that deals with identifying the components of substances and determining their composition.
